source.title: Attack and defense in rodents as ethoexperimental models for the study of emotion.

confidence_rationale: Foundational, extensively-cited ethoexperimental framework independently converging on the discreteness/predictability of threat as a feature that recruits a QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT behavioral complex (risk assessment) not seen for present/discrete threat -- directly relevant to the design question's threat-features sub-question, and a useful older, independent anchor alongside the more recent Fanselow-lineage entries. Confidence capped at moderate given the paper's age (1989) and its role here as background/converging-evidence rather than a load-bearing primary source.
failure_signatures: If REE's harm-valence signal is designed only to respond to DISCRETE, currently-active threat sources and has no way to represent a diffuse or POTENTIAL (not-yet-present) threat condition, it would miss this paper's core distinction: an important additional behavioral complex (risk assessment) is specifically elicited by nondiscrete/potential threat and is NOT seen for discrete, present threat -- these are functionally and behaviorally different regimes, not points on the same continuum treated identically.

If neuroanatomical/pharmacological manipulations of REE's future harm-selection pathway affect ALL harm-driven behaviors identically with no possibility of dissociating 'risk assessment'-like exploratory-cautious behavior from 'defensive threat/attack'-like committed behavior, that would be inconsistent with this paper's finding that real manipulations often have different, sometimes opposite, effects on offense/defense sub-components.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In an ethoexperimental framework distinguishing offense from defense in rodents, defensive behaviors are determined jointly by the threat stimulus AND the situation. Defense patterns elicited by a DISCRETE, approaching, present predator (or conspecific) threat share several behaviors in common with defense elicited by a NONDISCRETE, potential (not-yet-present, ambiguous) threat -- but the latter ADDITIONALLY includes an important risk-assessment behavioral complex (apprehensive expectation, vigilance, scanning) not seen for discrete, present threat. This risk-assessment complex shows considerable behavioral and functional similarity to generalized-anxiety symptomatology. Neuroanatomical and pharmacological manipulations frequently have different, sometimes opposite, effects on the offense vs. defense behavioral categories.
mapping.ree_translation: This is an early, independent (pre-PIC, though later cited by and consonant with it) anchor for the design question's threat-features sub-question: whether the threat is DISCRETE/present or NONDISCRETE/potential is itself a feature that recruits a qualitatively different behavioral complex (risk-assessment: cautious, exploratory, vigilant), not merely a difference in the magnitude of the same response. For REE's SD-hazard-aware-policy-decomposition, this reinforces (independently of the Fanselow-lineage predictability argument in this pull) that a mature harm-valence-weighted selection step should be able to represent and respond differently to a DIFFUSE/AMBIGUOUS harm signal (broader, more exploratory candidate consideration -- closer to REE's existing structural decompose/keep test) versus a DISCRETE/CONFIRMED harm signal (narrower, more committed selection toward a specific low-harm tile) -- i.e. discreteness/certainty of the harm source is a candidate second input dimension alongside raw magnitude, not something magnitude alone can substitute for.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a classical (1989) ethoexperimental framework paper, predating and independent of the specific PIC terminology used elsewhere in this pull, describing whole-organism offense/defense behavioral categories in rodents rather than any internal computational/circuit mechanism. Its relevance to REE's redecomposition-selection junction is at the level of 'discreteness/predictability of the threat source is a behaviorally consequential feature, distinct from magnitude' -- a conceptual point, not a mechanism or functional form REE could implement directly.
mapping.source_context: Ethoexperimental review, laboratory and semi-naturalistic rat behavior, foundational offense/defense behavioral taxonomy work from the Blanchard lab; frequently cited progenitor literature for the later Fanselow PIC framework.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, highly-cited classical ethoexperimental work, independently converging with the more recent Fanselow-lineage entries on discreteness/predictability as a distinct threat feature. Mapping fidelity moderate given its age and whole-organism-behavior scope; included as an independent corroborating anchor for the predictability dimension rather than as a primary load-bearing source.
